data.body: Investigated 2026-10-24 (read-only, not claimed; needs an operator decision on the trust model before code). Confirmed in code: _opcert_trust_root (src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py) is exclusive. When the cert's principal is this environment's own principal and the current own key exists, it returns only the own key and never reads the pinned keyring, so an envelope signed by the pre-rotation key verifies as mismatch. Not reproduced end to end (needs a signed envelope under the old key). Two things the ticket's criteria leave open: (1) the foreign-principal path (_pinned_environment_keys) already trusts every pinned key, revoked ones included, and checks no era; era checks (added_at_log_position / revoked_at_log_position, key_not_valid_at_era) live in verify_required_environment and need the cert's tickets-log position, which verify_opcert_record does not have. (2) A minimal fix, own key plus the pinned UNREVOKED keys for the same principal, is stricter than the foreign path but still cannot reject a key that was pinned later than the cert. Decision needed: accept unrevoked pinned keys only (simple, no era), or thread the cert's log position into verify_opcert_record so era applies here too (larger, changes a shared verification signature).
